thread_text:
Alex Nguyen: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands runtime portion — wanted to capture a few clarifying Qs about kernel rollout, KV cache behavior, and batching defaults. I'll list them, please ping if you want to take any.

Priya Desai: Thanks Alex — this is useful. I'll answer kernel + KV cache, Maya can chime on timeline and SLAs.

Alex Nguyen: Q1: Will kernel-v4 become the default on hosted before end of Q2? Some customers asked whether we'll flip traffic automatically.

Maya Torres: Short answer: not an automatic global flip. Plan is staged canary in late May on non-critical clusters, then opt-in for Dedicated in June, and a controlled full rollout (global default) in July if canaries look good. We'll publish a rollout schedule on the Console (releases tab) with canary windows and rollback hooks. :calendar:

Sam Patel: For the canary, what metrics are we watching? CPU/GPU utilization? p95/p99 latency? quality regressions?

Priya Desai: We have a short health checklist: p99 latency delta <= +5% on matching load, error rate < 0.1% increase, token cost variance within 3%, and no automated quality regressions on the regression suite (eval prompts). Also GPU memory regressions flagged. If any check fails we abort and notify infra leads.

Alex Nguyen: Q2: KV cache eviction — some users saw their warmup ineffective because cache evicted aggressively. What's the recommended per-route policy? TTL vs size-based?

Priya Desai: We recommend size-first with soft TTL. Default behavior will be LRU with a configurable `max_entries` and `soft_ttl_ms`. Example defaults we're rolling out: `max_entries: 50000`, `soft_ttl_ms: 3600000` (1h). Eviction is size-triggered; items older than soft_ttl become lower priority. We'll add explicit per-tenant overrides in the Console soon.

Katie Huang: Is there an operator knob to prefer prefix-caching for chat flows? Some customers want prefix retention even if entries are old.

Priya Desai: Yes — `prefetch_policy: prefix_strong` will pin prefixes up to `retain_size` and bypass soft_ttl for those keys. Example config snippet we're testing:

```
kv_cache:
  max_entries: 100000
  soft_ttl_ms: 7200000
  prefetch_policy: prefix_strong
  retain_size: 2000
```

Maya Torres: We're adding a Console toggle for `prefix_strong` in the next console patch (ETA mid-May) for Dedicated and Hosted tiers.

Alex Nguyen: Q3: Batching window defaults — we left the question open in the meeting about default 20ms vs 50ms for bursty workloads. Any guidance?

Sam Patel: Empirically: 20ms is better for latency-sensitive endpoints where p95 matters; 50ms gives ~1.6x throughput improvement for high token-rate pipelines with steady load. We're going to expose `batch_window_ms` per route with a recommended profile: `interactive:20`, `api-bulk:50`. Also will ship dynamic-adaptive batching that widens the window under sustained load.

Alex Nguyen: Will adaptive batching be enabled by default?

Priya Desai: Disabled by default for now. It's in canary with two customers. We want to avoid unintended latency bumps for low-volume apps. Toggle will be in Console and via API `runtime.features.adaptive_batching=true`.

Katie Huang: Any changes to default quantization profiles tied to kernel-v4? Customers noticed smaller memory but some quality fuzz.

Priya Desai: kernel-v4 adds a new `q-int8-mixed` profile that we're recommending for latency-sensitive production (mostly equivalent quality to int8 but about 20% faster for short contexts). We'll keep `q-int8` and `q-int4` for cost-oriented profiles. We're surfacing model-specific recommended profiles in the catalog UI.

Alex Nguyen: Action items: (1) Maya to publish rollout schedule + SLAs by EOW, (2) Priya to update docs with KV config examples and add Console toggle roadmap, (3) Sam to publish batching benchmark notes and recommended defaults, (4) Katie to follow up with customer-facing note on quant profiles. I can collect and make a short summary for the all-hands notes.

Maya Torres: Confirmed. I'll post the schedule and add a small FAQ about rollback and opt-in.

ops-bot: New release note created: "canary/kernel-v4" assigned to Priya Desai, due 2026-05-03.

Sam Patel: If anyone needs synthetic load tests for kernel-v4 canaries ping me, I have a small suite that simulates mixed short/long contexts.

Alex Nguyen: Great — thanks everyone. I'll ping the doc link here when I create the summary. :thumbsup:
